value.body: A medical writer turns clinical and scientific information into clear documents: study reports, regulatory submissions, journal manuscripts, and educational material for doctors or patients. Employers include pharma companies, clinical research organisations and medical communications agencies. A typical day involves reading studies, drafting and revising text, and checking every statement against its source.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BDS, Pharm.D, B.Pharm, MBBS, BHMS or life-science postgraduates

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Word processors, reference managers, literature databases

items.label: Pharma industry turnover
items.note: Pharma companies and CROs are the main employers of medical writers
items.source: Department of Pharmaceuticals Annual Report 2025-26 (as reported)

items.label: Trials on the Clinical Trials Registry-India
items.note: Cumulative since the registry began; each record needs written study documents
items.source: CTRI figures cited in a published analysis (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually enter as trainee or associate medical writers after a writing test. A short course in medical writing and a few writing samples (such as literature summaries) help. Clinical training in BDS or Pharm.D supports understanding of the content.

value.title: At a glance
items: Work is desk-based and can be done remotely in some firms.
Next roles: senior medical writer, publication or regulatory writing lead.

competition.note: BDS graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
